sources.entry: Stirling-PDF - Local hosted web application that allows you to perform various operations on PDF files, such as merging, splitting, file conversions and OCR. Apache-2.0 Docker/Java
Stirling-PDF - Locally hosted web application that allows you to perform various operations on PDF files
Stirling-PDF | Web-based PDF toolkit to merge, split, convert, OCR and sign PDFs

summary.one_liner: Stirling PDF is an open-source, self-hostable PDF editing platform offering a browser UI, desktop app, and REST API for editing, merging, splitting, converting, OCR, signing, and redacting PDFs.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Stirling PDF as a PDF editing platform that can run as a personal desktop app, in the browser, or on your own server with a private API. It advertises over 50 PDF tools covering editing, merging, splitting, signing, redaction, conversion, OCR, and compression. It also mentions no-code automation pipelines configurable in the UI and REST APIs for nearly all tools. The interface is said to be available in 40+ languages. The README states that documents are processed without being sent to external services. Enterprise features such as SSO and auditing are mentioned as part of a paid server plan. Quick start is a single Docker run command that serves the app on port 8080.
use_cases: convert documents to and from PDF
self-host a PDF tool for a team
automate PDF processing through an API
how_to_run: Open the web UI at http://localhost:8080 in a browser
For desktop and Kubernetes installs, see the Documentation Guide
Development: install Task and run `task dev` to start the editor (per the README)
notable: Runs as a desktop app, browser UI, or self-hosted server with a private API
50+ PDF tools including redaction, signing, and OCR
No-code automation pipelines configurable in the UI
Uses Task as a unified command runner for build, dev, and test
caveats: The README describes the project as open-core; enterprise features such as SSO and auditing are tied to a paid Server Plan & Enterprise tier
Desktop and Kubernetes installation details are deferred to external documentation
